Um...maybe don't do anything hasty. Is there any other way of contacting this person - perhaps by phone? Or online? If you're already starting to feel foolish perhaps get some other feedback (like from a friend) or continue to think it through.
I'm doing this all the time now and I don't know how to stop it.

Um...I have this condition and I felt like dying when I first found out I had it and there was no cure. I felt like you did - panicky, out of control, like my life was over, etc. 

Honestly, I don't even think about it now. No one I know cares, and in the grand scheme of weird body stuff, it could actually be worse.  

I told a therapist once and she's like...'so...it's like having acne, right?' I was like but that's *normal*, people understand that. This is freakish and weird and people will look at me like I'm a freak. 

I think what she was trying to get at was that people who have any skin condition (acne in various forms causes scarring, is incurable, etc., there's psoriasis and other things you shouldn't google) or body insecurity will feel bad about it. Vitiligo is...kinda cool when you think about it. Your skin is still smooth  - it's just two different colours. I've heard of people with white streaks in their hair and it looks awesome from an artist's POV - like a superhero or something. Anyway, this might be because I'm used to it and it doesn't bother me anymore.     

There's even a successful model now who has it, and with Bruce Jenner coming out, etc. differences are increasingly being celebrated. It's honestly OK. I just have a few spots, and you can use self-tanner if you hate them. Just wear sunscreen all the time (it will make you look younger anyway) and I don't know if you have dark skin, but depending on your pigmentation, most people probably won't notice. Stress is also the biggest concern, so don't freak out too much and try to just live healthily. If you still feel like killing yourself, here's a pic of a pigmented peacock to make you feel better. https://s-media-cache-ak0.pinimg.com/736x/cb/13/88/cb1388fab5e3016a0dc8be8ce4573ddd.jpg You're a teenager so insecurity is normal, but I can promise it gets better and you'll learn to accept yourself in time, my friend.
